claims.text: The initial material is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy, exemplified by a WxTaTiVCr system.
Spark plasma sintering can produce the proposed homogeneous baseline microstructure without deliberate nanoprecipitates.
A stepwise post-sintering heat treatment will induce coherent nanoprecipitates in the alloy.
High-temperature TEM or synchrotron XRD can track precipitate size and coherence during treatment or testing.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1000 °C are representative of relevant fusion plasma-facing high-temperature conditions.
The heat treatment can create coherent nanoprecipitates with stable, well-defined interfaces that persist at 800–1000 °C.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as local stress-relief sites.
Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate smooth or continuous dislocation transmission.
Stress relief and continuous dislocation transmission reduce local stress concentrations.
Reduced local stress concentrations delay strain localization.
Reduced local stress concentrations delay crack initiation.
An alloy containing coherent nanoprecipitates will have greater high-temperature plastic strain capacity than the untreated baseline.
An alloy containing coherent nanoprecipitates will have greater toughness than the untreated baseline.
The nanoprecipitate-containing alloy will exhibit delayed strain localization and a more uniform stress-strain response.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the nanoprecipitates remain coherent and stable at approximately 800–1000 °C.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherence places the material outside the stated validity boundary.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that coarsening or loss of precipitate coherence is outside the domain in which the hypothesis should hold, whereas the falsification rule treats rapid coarsening or loss of coherence as directly falsifying the hypothesis. Failure to maintain the stipulated mediator would test the intervention or boundary condition rather than decisively refute the conditional mechanism.
